influences.name: Trevor Horn
influences.context: Trevor's a very inspiring producer, actually. I've never quite come across anybody who has the ability to get the best out of people like Trevor does

influences.name: Earth, Wind & Fire
influences.context: He'd send me a rough mix of a Dollar track and a note saying, 'I want brass on the chorus — Earth, Wind & Fire; and strings for the verse — Barry Manilow.'

influences.name: Barry Manilow
influences.context: He'd send me a rough mix of a Dollar track and a note saying, 'I want brass on the chorus — Earth, Wind & Fire; and strings for the verse — Barry Manilow.'

influences.name: Bach
influences.context: I used to love those pieces where Bach uses a hymn tune and does this wonderful counterpoint all around it. The most simple example I can give you would be 'Jesu Joy of Man's Desiring'

influences.name: Phillip Glass
influences.context: I thought, 'Well, suppose I put around it that very repetitive, percussive sort of counterpoint that people like Phillip Glass use.' Because I love that music, I love those 'minimalists'

influences.name: John Adams
influences.context: I suppose that was my closest homage to John Adams and the minimalists

influences.name: Hindemith
influences.context: I once read a very good book by a composer called Hindemith in which he described how, when you start a piece, you do have this very strong picture in your head as to how it should be

influences.name: Paul Simon
influences.context: For instance, Paul Simon throughout his career has taken whatever elements of whatever culture he wants and used them in his own songs, and his songs are so strong that it's always worked
